clues.text: Standing 154 feet tall, this non-inverting steel coaster hits a top speed of 66 mph.
This coaster was built by the manufacturer Intamin and made its grand debut in 2002.
This coaster is located in the Netherlands at a park that was once part of the Six Flags chain, a legacy that explains why several other coasters in the world share its name.
Formerly the fastest and tallest coaster in the Benelux region, this steel ride at Walibi Holland is well-known for its cable lift hill and an overbanked element called a Stengel Dive.
This coaster's name refers to a biblical giant from Gath who was famously defeated by David and his sling.

evidence.quote: At this time, the park was owned by Six Flags, who have named several of their roller coasters 'Goliath'.

It was previously described as "the fastest, highest, and longest coaster in the Benelux". Since 2021, both these records belong to Kondaa in Walibi Belgium. ... it ascends a hill called a Stengel Dive, the top being overbanked to around 100° to the right
Goliath is a steel roller coaster located at the Walibi Holland theme park in Biddinghuizen, Dronten, in the Netherlands.
